narrative.overview:
The interface is the Ministry's reception desk. It welcomes you, it is composed and it is unhurried. It reads as official without being cold. A visitor standing in the lobby, phone in hand, and a receptionist working through a morning rush should both feel that the desk has things in hand. Every screen answers "what do I do next?" before it says anything else.

The look is built from four things: one teal family carries identity and action; cool slate neutrals sit on a pale paper background; confident, heavy headings sit over plain, readable body text; and corners are generously rounded. Depth is layered and lifted. White cards sit on the paper background, rise on hover, and dialogs float well above everything else. The Ministry of Finance logo and seal are the identity marks. Real building and reception photography carries the visitor-facing welcome, and the staff tools stay quiet and dense.

Dark mode is a full sibling, not an afterthought. Slate is inverted at the token level, and teal shifts to its brighter steps so it still reads on navy.
keyCharacteristics: Colour: a single teal family for identity, action and data. Status hues (red, amber, emerald) are used only for state.
Type: headings and figures in the heaviest weight (900) with slightly tightened letter spacing; body text stays regular.
Shape: soft, generous corners. Cards are 24px, controls 12px, chips and avatars fully round.
Depth: layered, lifting surfaces. Cards lift and gently bob on hover; dialogs and hero panels cast deep, soft shadows.
Touch: large targets of at least 44px and 16px form text, built for phones first.

rules.name: The One Teal Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only brand colour. The former yellow-gold accent (#fcd116) has been removed from the system. Do not reintroduce gold, a second brand hue or a gradient between colours.

rules.name: The Fill-Behind-White Rule
rules.body: Any solid teal fill that carries white text uses Teal Action (#115e59) or darker. Lighter teals are only for tints, borders, charts and text on dark surfaces.

rules.name: The Status-Is-Not-Brand Rule
rules.body: Red, amber and emerald appear only to report state. Every status colour comes with a text label or an icon, never colour alone.

rules.name: The Heavy Figures Rule
rules.body: Counts, KPIs and visit references are set at weight 900 with tabular numerals, so columns of figures line up and read at a glance.

rules.name: The Sixteen Floor Rule
rules.body: No input, select or textarea text is smaller than 16px. This stops iOS from zooming in and keeps the form readable in a lobby.

rules.name: The Lift-Means-Touchable Rule
rules.body: A surface lifts on hover only when clicking it does something. Static information cards keep the resting shadow.

rules.name: The Motion-Consent Rule
rules.body: Lifts, bobs and slide-ins run only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference. Without motion, depth is shown by shadow alone.

dos: Do use Teal Action (#115e59) or darker for any solid fill behind white text.
Do keep every touch target at least 44px and every form control's text at least 16px.
Do set counts and figures at weight 900 with tabular numerals.
Do give interactive cards the hover lift, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
Do add a dark-theme counterpart in src/dark-theme.css whenever a new light-only colour utility appears.
Do pair every status colour with a label or an icon.
Do use the Ministry of Finance logo and seal as the only identity marks.
donts: Don't reintroduce the yellow-gold accent (#fcd116) or any second brand hue.
Don't put white text on Teal Primary (#0d9488) or any lighter teal.
Don't use colour alone to show a status.
Don't add a bottom mobile navigation bar.
Don't use inline HTML styles in chart tooltips or injected markup; the Content-Security-Policy blocks them.
Don't add thick or coloured side borders to cards, list items or alerts.
Don't show real visitor data in screenshots, fixtures or design examples.
